P1.evidence: Referenced the setter but deliberately did not read the notes back — 'So he briefed me in on your situation. However, I'm kind of an old-school guy, and I prefer to hear directly from a person.' The frame was three-part not four ('what you're trying to achieve, how we can help you doing that, and if there's an alignment'), with no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. No frame-agreement question was asked. The open question ran: 'So brief me in, like what's going on, like how it can help you.'

P2.evidence: Strongest phase of the call. Work ('what do you do, like, on a daily basis in terms of work?'), injuries ('do you have, like, any injuries from the past or recent or anything that limits your movements?'), training week, results ('So you've been stuck in this weight for how long?'), diet ('brief me in also on the nutrition part... do you follow any specific diet'), sleep ('How is your sleep routine? Do you sleep well?... And you wake up rested, energized?') and energy ('how about the energy throughout the day?') all ran. Weight and age were volunteered rather than asked; height was drawn out indirectly ('You look like a tall guy, too'). Health conditions, own or hereditary, were never asked — only injuries.

P3.evidence: The bridge landed: 'if you would, like, have to say in your own words, like, what's the biggest why?' produced 'just, you know, my self-esteem'. The rep then drove to others well — 'Do you want to play with them, or do you want to be the granddad that sits on the couch all day?' — and the prospect reached legacy himself: 'it's not only about the physique, but staying healthy for them too.' Weakness is that the deeper goal questions were led rather than opened: 'I can imagine we were playing the long-term game, the longevity game. Is that correct?' assumes the answer. 'When you're moving better, what does that actually do for you?' was never asked, and the reflect-back was a restatement rather than a check ('So it's not only about the physique').

P4.evidence: 'Do you have any ideas what could be the reason why you're stuck at it?' is a clean P4d and produced steps and late-night eating. But the past-attempts chain was never worked: the $300/month HIIT gym and the switch came out unprompted, the rep only asked 'what kind of workouts that you were doing?' after the fact, and never asked what happened with it or why it did not stick. The accountability gap — the single most useful thing the prospect said — was volunteered, not elicited: 'one thing about me is, you know, I have accountability. So when I feel like I'm accountable to somebody or something, I seem to do it more.' The information-isn't-the-problem line only appeared after the price objection: 'everything is out there... but the thing is, the structure, the program, that's the essence.'

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was run before the offer. The closest thing is a single line after the price objection — 'you've been trying to do that for years, and I don't want to leave you, and again, being stuck at this weight and not hitting it' — which is the rep's assertion, not the prospect's own two-year picture. He was never asked whether he was willing to settle for it, never asked why not, and never asked to draw a line in the sand. The price therefore landed with no cost of inaction behind it, against a prospect who is comfortable, sleeping well and already training five days a week.

P6.evidence: P6a ran cleanly: 'if you had this right training, the simple nutrition and accountability from Trevor, do you agree that you would get finally to that dream physique and become mobile, stronger for your future self and for your grandkids?' The answer was hedged — 'Yeah. I believe it could work if I think. Yeah. He could be the right person to motivate me into that' — and the rep moved straight to the investment anyway rather than returning to Phase 5. The go-all-in question was only asked after the price objection, as an isolate: 'apart from the money... do you feel you would actually want to do this?'

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but the prospect declined at price and again after each restructure, so payment, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement and the welcome-email steps were never reachable. The rep did pre-frame the onboarding call earlier ('There's only one, the first session, the onboarding session with Trevor'), which is correct sequencing, but nothing in P11 was executed.

objection_plays.detail: The isolate ran — 'money is like the logistical part of it, but apart from the money, is there anything that would be... do you feel you would actually want to do this?' — and the payment-plan opener ran in substance ('what I could offer you is to break it in half with no interest on that'). Everything else was skipped. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. No permission question about having an open, honest conversation about his finances. None of the six financial-picture questions ran: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus after bills, no number of credit cards, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no crypto or investments. The prospect volunteered a budget ceiling of '2-3' and the rep took it at face value and started cutting the offer instead of opening the wallet.

'Let me think about it and see how I can possibly work that number' and later 'I think I'm going to have to think about this a little longer' both landed. None of the play ran — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here'. The rep answered a decision objection with a discount.

Script gap, not a rep failure. The prospect's anchor is Primal's own free content plus a cheap gym, and it is demonstrably working for him: 'I've seen my arms and everything, my change since I've been doing the kettlebells, which has been about two months' and 'I'll keep using Trevor's videos.' This is the same gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call — Objection C assumes capacity to pay is the blocker, not a functioning low-cost substitute. The rep improvised an information-versus-structure reframe, which is the right instinct but has no scripted support and did not survive contact.

notes: Baseline discovery was genuinely good and the grandkids thread was well driven — but the rep went from a hedged commitment answer straight to price with no consequence frame at all, so there was nothing to weigh $6,000 against. When the objection came he discounted rather than opened the wallet: three new commercial structures in under six minutes and not one financial-picture question. Coach the P5-to-P6 sequence and the discipline to run OC's financial picture before touching the price.
